# ECCR Picture Book Technical Handoff

## 1. Purpose

This document allows another LLM or developer to understand, reproduce, and safely maintain the ECCR Picture Book application without access to the original conversation history.

Current production locations:

- Picture Book: `https://jieunjanetsong.github.io/eccr-picture-audio-site/picturebook/`
- Audio Practice: `https://jieunjanetsong.github.io/eccr-picture-audio-site/audio/`
- GitHub repository: `https://github.com/JiEunJanetSong/eccr-picture-audio-site`

The current deployment contains `Book1` through `Book7`.

## 2. Product Definition

ECCR Picture Book is a static, web-based reading tool designed to work on low-spec smartphones and standard desktop computers in Ghana.

The main user flow is:

1. The learner selects a book.
2. The learner taps a printed word, sentence, or heading on the page image.
3. The teacher recording mapped to that exact text plays.
4. The learner moves between pages using the page numbers or previous/next controls.
5. While online, the learner selects `Save offline` and waits for `Offline ready`.
6. The books and recordings can then be used offline in the same browser or installed home-screen app.

The project also provides an `Audio Practice` view that presents the same content as a selectable list.

### Requirements That Must Be Preserved

- The application name is `ECCR`.
- Keep the `Produced by Team Kairos` credit visible.
- Do not require login, accounts, or a database.
- The application must remain deployable as static files.
- Packaged teacher recordings must work when the developer's MacBook and local TTS server are off.
- The UI must work on mobile phones and desktop computers.
- When a page contains both Twi and English, each language must play the recording for that language.
- Do not replace missing recordings with incorrect TTS. The current UI displays `Audio coming soon`.
- Hotspots must be invisible so the learner appears to tap the printed text itself.
- Moving quickly between text items must not leave a translucent box or stale playing state.
- Changing the book or page must stop the current audio immediately.

## 3. Technology Stack

- HTML5
- CSS3
- Vanilla JavaScript
- HTML `<audio>` element
- Web App Manifest
- Service Worker and Cache Storage API
- Node.js scripts for generating the offline asset list and checking JavaScript syntax
- GitHub Pages and GitHub Actions for production deployment
- Netlify and Vercel configuration files are included, but GitHub Pages is the current production host.

The frontend has no framework, bundler, database, authentication layer, or required server runtime. This reduces startup cost and maintenance complexity on low-spec devices.

## 4. Repository Layout

```text
eccr-picture-audio-site/
├── .github/workflows/pages.yml       # Deploys main to GitHub Pages
├── audio/
│   ├── index.html                    # List-based Audio Practice UI
│   ├── app.js
│   └── style.css
├── icons/icon.svg                    # PWA icon
├── picturebook/
│   ├── assets/
│   │   ├── book1/page-01.jpg ...
│   │   └── book7/page-12.jpg
│   ├── audio/
│   │   ├── book1/*.mp3 ...
│   │   └── book7/*.mp3
│   ├── a4_books.js                   # Shared content, hotspot, and audio data
│   ├── app.js                        # Picture Book runtime
│   ├── index.html
│   └── style.css
├── scripts/generate-offline-assets.mjs
├── shared/config.js                  # Optional TTS API policy
├── index.html                        # App selection page
├── manifest.webmanifest
├── offline-assets.js                 # Generated file; do not edit manually
├── pwa.js                            # Save Offline UI and SW messages
├── sw.js                             # Offline cache and MP3 range responses
├── MISSING_VOICE_RECORDINGS.md       # Visible text without recordings
├── package.json
```

There are currently 112 page images:

- Book1: 12 pages
- Book2: 20 pages
- Book3: 32 pages

## 5. Shared Content Data Contract

`picturebook/a4_books.js` is the main content source. It creates the `window.ECCR_A4_BOOKS` array, which is consumed by both Picture Book and Audio Practice.

### Book Object

```js
{
  id: "book7",
  title: "Book7",
  assetDir: "assets/book7",
  pages: [/* Page objects */]
}
```

Rules:

- `id` must be unique. The recommended format is `bookN`.
- Books are sorted numerically using the number found in `id` or `title`.
- Current display titles use `Book1`, `Book2`, and so on.
- `assetDir` is relative to `picturebook/index.html`.

### Page Object

```js
{
  title: "Simple Sentences",
  image: "page-04.jpg",
  audio: [/* AudioItem objects */]
}
```

Blank pages must remain in the data so that page order matches the printed book.

```js
{
  title: "Blank",
  image: "page-10.jpg",
  audio: []
}
```

### AudioItem Object

Normal item with a recording:

```js
{
  text: "Sam has a cap.",
  speechText: "Sam has a cap.",
  audioSrc: "audio/book7/page-04-01.mp3",
  box: { x: 47, y: 28, w: 36, h: 8 },
  lang: "en"
}
```

One recording mapped to two separate printed regions:

```js
{
  text: "Writing Activity: Write",
  speechText: "Writing Activity: Write",
  audioSrc: "audio/book7/page-09-heading.mp3",
  boxes: [
    { x: 28, y: 8, w: 44, h: 7 },
    { x: 16, y: 23, w: 20, h: 7 }
  ],
  lang: "en"
}
```

Visible text without a recording:

```js
{
  text: "Short /a/ Reader",
  speechText: "Short /a/ Reader",
  box: { x: 32, y: 20, w: 36, h: 6 },
  lang: "en",
  recordingMissing: true
}
```

Field definitions:

| Field | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | Yes | Text used in lists and accessibility labels |
| `speechText` | Recommended | Spoken text and recording reference text |
| `audioSrc` | For recordings | Teacher recording path relative to `picturebook/` |
| `box` | Conditional | One tappable region |
| `boxes` | Conditional | Multiple regions that play the same recording |
| `lang` | Yes | `twi`, `en`, or occasionally `twi-en` |
| `recordingMissing` | For missing audio | Prevents TTS and shows the pending-audio state |

Every item should have either `box` or `boxes`. The application can estimate a temporary box from text length, but production books must use manually verified coordinates.

## 6. Hotspot Coordinate System

Hotspots use percentages of the full page image rather than image pixels.

```text
x = leftPixel / imageWidth * 100
y = topPixel / imageHeight * 100
w = boxWidth / imageWidth * 100
h = boxHeight / imageHeight * 100
```

For example, a rectangle beginning at `(560, 472)` with a size of `(430, 135)` on a 1191 x 1684 image becomes:

```js
{
  x: 560 / 1191 * 100,
  y: 472 / 1684 * 100,
  w: 430 / 1191 * 100,
  h: 135 / 1684 * 100
}
```

Percentage coordinates keep hotspots aligned with responsive page images on both phones and desktops.

Hotspot rules:

- Include modest padding around the letters for finger input.
- Do not overlap adjacent words or sentences.
- A sentence hotspot should cover the entire printed sentence.
- Add a separate item for a heading when a heading recording exists.
- Keep hotspot backgrounds, focus outlines, and mobile tap highlights invisible.
- Verify coordinates at both mobile and desktop widths.

## 7. Audio Routing and Playback Priority

`picturebook/app.js` and `audio/app.js` resolve audio in this order:

1. If `recordingMissing` is `true`, do not play anything and show `Audio coming soon`.
2. If `audioSrc` exists, play the packaged teacher recording.
3. If neither condition applies and a TTS API is configured, build a TTS URL based on `lang`.
4. If no source is available, do not play audio.

On GitHub Pages, `shared/config.js` deliberately leaves the TTS API URL empty:

```js
window.ECCR_STATIC_AUDIO_ONLY = window.location.hostname.endsWith("github.io");
window.ECCR_TTS_API_BASE = window.ECCR_STATIC_AUDIO_ONLY ? "" : window.location.origin;
```

The production app therefore plays its packaged MP3 files without depending on an external TTS service or local MacBook.

Current behavior to understand:

- Changing the English or Twi voice does not alter packaged teacher recordings.
- Voice selectors matter only when a deployment has a TTS backend and an item needs synthesis.
- The default English TTS fallback is Kokoro `bm_fable` at speed `0.9`.
- The default Twi TTS fallback is MMS Akan/Twi `mms-aka` at speed `0.9`.
- `recordingMissing` intentionally disables fallback synthesis to prevent incorrect pronunciation.

### Relative Path Difference Between the Two Apps

For the same `audioSrc` value:

- Picture Book uses `item.audioSrc` directly because it runs inside `picturebook/`.
- Audio Practice resolves it as `../picturebook/${item.audioSrc}` because it runs inside `audio/`.

Changing this rule can break audio in one app while leaving the other app operational.

## 8. Pages Containing Twi and English

Do not connect one combined recording to separate Twi and English lines. Split the recording and create one hotspot per language.

```js
function bilingualPage(bookNumber, pageNumber, twi, english) {
  const base = `audio/book${bookNumber}/page-${String(pageNumber).padStart(2, "0")}`;
  return page(pageNumber, twi, [
    recording(twi, `${base}-twi.mp3`, TWI_BOX, "twi"),
    recording(english, `${base}-en.mp3`, ENGLISH_BOX, "en"),
  ]);
}
```

Recommended filenames:

```text
page-03-twi.mp3
page-03-en.mp3
```

Use one file with `lang: "twi-en"` only when the source recording intentionally alternates between Twi and English as one inseparable item, such as a bilingual question block.

## 9. PDF and Page Image Processing

The app does not render PDFs in the browser. Every PDF page is converted to a JPEG before deployment.

Current image conventions:

- Filenames: `page-01.jpg`, `page-02.jpg`, and so on
- Page numbers use two-digit zero padding.
- Current final pages are 1191 x 1684 JPEG images.
- CSS fixes the page ratio with `aspect-ratio: 816 / 1158`.

Example conversion with Poppler:

```sh
mkdir -p picturebook/assets/book8
pdftoppm -jpeg -r 144 -jpegopt quality=82 \
  /path/to/ECCR_Book_8.pdf \
  /tmp/book8-page
```

Rename and move the output into `picturebook/assets/book8/` using the project naming convention. When a source PDF is replaced, page count, page order, and text positions may change. Inspect every page and do not reuse old hotspot coordinates without verification.

## 10. Recording Segmentation and Text Matching

When a source recording contains a full page or full book, divide it into the smallest useful units represented by tappable text.

Recommended process:

1. Extract all visible PDF text in page order.
2. Listen to the full recording and identify the start and end time of each visible item.
3. Use a local ASR model such as Whisper only to produce draft timestamps.
4. Manually verify Ghanaian English, Twi, and children's reading because ASR errors are likely.
5. Exclude greetings, instructions, page announcements, `Thank you`, and other narration not printed in the book.
6. Reuse one clip when exactly the same title appears on multiple pages with identical pronunciation.
7. Create separate clips when individual words must be independently tappable.
8. Check each final clip for excessive silence, clipped phonemes, and click noise.

FFmpeg example:

```sh
ffmpeg -y -i source.m4a -ss 12.40 -to 14.85 \
  -codec:a libmp3lame -b:a 96k \
  picturebook/audio/book8/page-03-01.mp3
```

Validation example:

```sh
ffprobe -v error -show_entries format=duration \
  -of default=noprint_wrappers=1:nokey=1 \
  picturebook/audio/book8/page-03-01.mp3
```

MP3 is the preferred deployment format because it is small and broadly compatible. M4A and WAV are acceptable source formats, but the deployed package should normally contain MP3 files only.

## 11. Adding a New Book

Follow this order:

1. Confirm the source PDF page count and page order.
2. Render every page to JPEG and inspect the images visually.
3. Place images in `picturebook/assets/bookN/`.
4. Inventory all source recordings and their durations.
5. Match the printed text to the recordings page by page.
6. Split recordings into sentence or word clips where required.
7. Place final MP3 files in `picturebook/audio/bookN/`.
8. Add Book, Page, and AudioItem data to `picturebook/a4_books.js`.
9. Use `missing(...)` for visible text that has no recording.
10. Add all missing items to `MISSING_VOICE_RECORDINGS.md`.
11. Run `npm run build:offline`.
12. Increment the service worker cache name and both HTML asset query versions.
13. Validate syntax, file references, playback, mobile hotspots, and offline behavior.
14. Commit and push to `main` to deploy through GitHub Pages.

Minimal book example:

```js
{
  id: "book8",
  title: "Book8",
  assetDir: "assets/book8",
  pages: [
    page(1, "Book title", [
      recording("Book title", "audio/book8/title.mp3", COVER_BOX, "en"),
    ]),
    page(2, "Sentence Practice", [
      recording(
        "This is a sentence.",
        "audio/book8/page-02-01.mp3",
        { x: 15, y: 60, w: 70, h: 8 },
        "en"
      ),
    ]),
  ],
}
```

## 12. Picture Book Runtime

Main state in `picturebook/app.js`:

```js
{
  bookId,
  pageIndex,
  audio,
  playbackToken,
  englishVoice,
  twiVoice
}
```

Important behavior:

- Changing books selects page 1, stops audio, and rerenders the screen.
- Changing pages stops audio and rerenders the image, title, counter, and hotspots.
- Tapping text stops the previous recording before starting the new one.
- `playbackToken` prevents delayed `ended` or `error` events from an old recording from clearing a newer playing state.
- Left Arrow selects the previous page.
- Right Arrow or Space selects the next page.
- Mobile hides the left/right page buttons and uses the numbered navigation below the book.

Hotspots are absolutely positioned buttons over the page image. They have `title` and `aria-label` attributes but remain visually transparent.

## 13. Audio Practice Runtime

The `audio/` app uses the same `ECCR_A4_BOOKS` data and provides:

- Book selection
- A selectable page list
- A list of all audio items on the page
- An individual `Listen` control
- A `Play page` action that plays page items in order

`sequenceToken` cancels an earlier page-play sequence when the user changes context or starts another action.

## 14. Responsive UI Requirements

Picture Book on desktop:

- Use a three-row layout: header, centered page, and bottom page navigation.
- Fit the page to both viewport height and width, with a maximum width of 720px.
- Show previous and next page controls at the sides.

Picture Book on mobile (`max-width: 820px`):

- Do not use a fixed header. It must scroll away so it does not cover the book.
- Rearrange header controls into two columns.
- Let the book selector and status use full width.
- Fit the page to screen width and remove the desktop shadow and rounded corners.
- Hide side page controls.
- Keep the numbered page controls large enough for touch.

Target browsers:

- Current Safari, Chrome, and Edge
- iPhone/iPad through Safari or Add to Home Screen
- Android through Chrome or installed PWA
- Standard Windows desktops, including HP computers, through Chrome or Edge

## 15. PWA and Offline Architecture

### File Responsibilities

- `manifest.webmanifest`: installation name, start URL, scope, and standalone display
- `pwa.js`: service worker registration, save requests, and progress UI
- `offline-assets.js`: generated list of all files required offline
- `sw.js`: cache population, version cleanup, fetch handling, and media ranges

### Offline Save Flow

1. The page registers root-level `sw.js`.
2. During installation, the worker attempts to cache the core files and the full offline package.
3. Selecting `Save offline` sends `CACHE_ALL_OFFLINE_ASSETS`.
4. The worker downloads only missing files in batches of four.
5. The worker reports progress with `OFFLINE_PROGRESS`.
6. The UI displays `Offline ready` after every asset is present.
7. Same-origin requests are then served cache-first.

### MP3 Range Requests

Safari and Chrome can request audio using the HTTP `Range` header. Returning an ordinary cached response may cause offline MP3 playback to fail.

`createRangeResponse()` in `sw.js` slices the cached Blob and returns `206 Partial Content` with:

- `Accept-Ranges`
- `Content-Length`
- `Content-Range`
- `Content-Type`

Do not remove this logic.

### User Instructions

```text
To use the app without an internet connection, click Save Offline while you are online and wait until Offline Ready appears. After that, you can access the books and audio offline using the same browser. This works the same way on desktop computers.
```

On iPhone, users can open the site in Safari and select Share > Add to Home Screen. The initial download must finish while connected to the internet. The learner must continue using the same browser profile or installed home-screen app.

Offline data can be removed if the browser evicts storage or the user clears site data.

## 16. Cache Updates After Content Changes

After changing any image, MP3, HTML, CSS, or JavaScript file:

1. Regenerate the offline list:

```sh
npm run build:offline
```

2. Change `CACHE_NAME` in `sw.js` to a new unique value:

```js
const CACHE_NAME = "eccr-final-books-YYYYMMDD-N";
```

3. Update the matching `?v=` query values in `picturebook/index.html` and `audio/index.html`.
4. Run `npm run check` again.
5. After deployment, open the app online and select `Save offline` until `Offline ready` appears.

Without a new cache name, installed users can remain on old images or JavaScript. Never edit `offline-assets.js` manually because it is generated.

## 17. Local Development and Verification

Run from the repository root:

```sh
npm run check
npm run serve
```

Local addresses:

```text
http://localhost:4173/
http://localhost:4173/picturebook/
http://localhost:4173/audio/
```

Do not open the HTML directly through `file://`; service workers and relative paths require an HTTP server.

### Minimum Verification Checklist

- `npm run check` passes.
- Every image referenced by `a4_books.js` exists.
- Every referenced `audioSrc` file exists.
- Books appear in ascending Book number order.
- Every page image appears in the correct order and aspect ratio.
- Every word, sentence, and heading hotspot is aligned correctly.
- Twi text plays Twi audio and English text plays English audio.
- Selecting another item immediately starts the new recording without stale UI state.
- Blank and credit pages do not contain accidental hotspots.
- The mobile header scrolls and does not obscure the book.
- `Save offline` reaches `Offline ready`.
- In airplane mode, fully close and reopen the app, then verify images and audio.
- Repeat offline testing on desktop in the same browser profile.

`npm run check` validates JavaScript syntax only. It does not verify referenced files, hotspot coordinates, playback correctness, or offline restart behavior. Those require additional checks and browser QA.

## 18. Deployment

`.github/workflows/pages.yml` deploys the static repository to GitHub Pages whenever `main` is pushed.

```sh
git status --short
git add <changed-files>
git commit -m "Describe the ECCR update"
git push origin main
```

Deployment verification:

```sh
gh run list --workflow pages.yml --limit 1
gh run watch <run-id>
```

An existing installation can briefly show the old version after a successful deployment because of its service worker cache. Verify the service worker cache name and HTML query versions first.

Netlify and Vercel can also serve the project without a build step. Use the repository root as the publish directory. HTTPS is required for service workers.

## 19. Missing Recordings

Use `MISSING_VOICE_RECORDINGS.md` as the authoritative list, including suggested filenames. Current missing items are:

- Book2 p17: `Kenkan bio.`
- Book3 p1/p2: `Asante Twi Reading Practice`
- Book3 p30: `Kenkan bio.`
- Book4 p1: `Aku and the Cat.`
- Book4 p10: `Kenkan bio.`
- Book4 p10: `Read again.`
- Book6 p1/p2: `Twi Letter Cards`
- Book7 p1/p2: `Short /a/ Reader`

When a new recording arrives:

1. Add it to the correct `picturebook/audio/bookN/` directory.
2. Replace the corresponding `missing(...)` item with `recording(...)`.
3. Remove the resolved row from `MISSING_VOICE_RECORDINGS.md`.
4. Regenerate the offline list and increment the cache version.
5. Verify playback both online and after a cold airplane-mode restart.

## 20. Known Constraints and Future Improvements

- Items without teacher recordings remain silent on the static GitHub Pages deployment.
- Voice selectors do not affect packaged recordings. A future static-only UI could hide them or label the source as `Recorded voice`.
- Downloading every book and recording at once will become slower and consume more storage as the library grows.
- For a larger library, provide separate `Save all books` and `Save selected book` actions.
- Hotspot coordinates are currently entered manually in code. If books are added frequently, create an admin tool that lets an editor click and drag over a page image to generate coordinates.
- Automated transcription is only a timestamping aid and must not be treated as final validation of Twi text or pronunciation.

## 21. Instructions for Another LLM

Use the following as the implementation prompt:

```text
You are maintaining the ECCR static picture-book PWA.
Read TECHNICAL_HANDOFF_EN.md, README.md, picturebook/a4_books.js,
picturebook/app.js, pwa.js, and sw.js before editing.

Use the existing data model and relative-path rules. Do not replace recorded
teacher audio with browser TTS. If visible text has no recording, mark it with
recordingMissing and update MISSING_VOICE_RECORDINGS.md. For bilingual pages,
map Twi and English text to separate language-correct clips and hotspots.

After every content or asset change, regenerate offline-assets.js, bump the
service-worker cache version and HTML asset query versions, run syntax and
reference checks, test desktop/mobile playback, and verify a cold offline
restart. Do not deploy until all referenced files return successfully.
```

## 22. Definition of Done

A new implementation or maintenance change is complete only when:

- Page images, order, and printed text match the supplied final PDF.
- Every hotspot is aligned with the actual printed text.
- Every hotspot plays only the correct language and recording.
- Packaged recordings work without an external server or developer laptop.
- The UI does not overlap or clip on mobile and desktop.
- The app can be fully reopened offline after its initial online save.
- Every changed asset is present in the offline list and a new cache version is deployed.
- The GitHub Pages workflow succeeds and the production URL is verified.

from pathlib import Path
import hashlib
import json
import random

import sys
from collections import Counter

from PIL import Image, ImageDraw
from reportlab.pdfgen import canvas
from reportlab.pdfbase import pdfmetrics
from reportlab.pdfbase.ttfonts import TTFont
from reportlab.lib.colors import HexColor, white
from reportlab.lib.pagesizes import A4
from reportlab.lib.units import mm

from reportlab.platypus import Paragraph
from reportlab.lib.styles import ParagraphStyle

ROOT=Path(__file__).resolve().parent
FINAL=ROOT.parent.parent/'최종'
ASSETS=ROOT/'assets'
QA=ROOT/'qa'
DATA=json.loads((ROOT/'manuscripts.json').read_text())
W,H=A4
GREEN=HexColor('#138754');DARK=HexColor('#126B46');INK=HexColor('#202923')
CREAM=HexColor('#FFFCF5');PALE=HexColor('#EAF4ED');BLUE=HexColor('#E7F2F6')
SAND=HexColor('#D8CCB7');MUTED=HexColor('#5D6C63');RED=HexColor('#D9535F')
FONTROOT=Path('/System/Library/Fonts/Supplemental')
for name,file in [('Body','Arial.ttf'),('Bold','Arial Bold.ttf'),('Display','Times New Roman Bold.ttf')]:
    pdfmetrics.registerFont(TTFont(name,str(FONTROOT/file)))
C=None;BOOK='';PAGE=0;LOG=[];ANSWERS={};LINE_BOXES=[]
HEART={'a','the','is','has','i'}
VOWELS=set('aeiou')


def words(s):return re.findall(r'[A-Za-z]+',s)
def digest(p):return hashlib.sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest()


def audit():
    records=[];alltexts=[]
    for book,bd in DATA['books'].items():
        known=set()
        for t in bd['texts']:
            if t['target']=='mixed':known=set('aeiou')
            else:known.add(t['target'])
            n=t['number'];expected=5 if n<=4 else 6 if n<=10 else 7
            assert len(t['sentences'])==expected,(t['id'],'sentence count')
            passage=' '.join(t['sentences']);alltexts.append(passage)
            terms=words(t['title']+' '+passage)+t['blend']
            for q in t['questions']:terms += [q['answer'],q['distractor']]
            for token in terms:
                token=token.lower()
                assert len(token)<=4,(t['id'],token,'length')
                if token in HEART:continue
                assert (set(token)&VOWELS)<=known,(t['id'],token,'untaught vowel')
                assert token=='and' or re.fullmatch(r'[bcdfghjklmnpqrstvwxyz]?[aeiou][bcdfghjklmnpqrstvwxyz]?',token),(t['id'],token,'outside VC/CVC + and')
            for item in t['blend']:
                assert len(item)==3 and item[1].lower() in VOWELS,(t['id'],item)
            hearts=[v for v in DATA['heart_words'] if v.lower() in {w.lower() for w in words(passage)}]
            t['hearts']=hearts
            chosen=next(v for v in reversed(t['blend']) if re.search(r'\b'+v+r'\b',passage,re.I))
            line=next(s for s in t['sentences'] if re.search(r'\b'+chosen+r'\b',s,re.I))
            match=re.search(r'\b'+chosen+r'\b',line,re.I)
            actual=match.group(0)
            cloze=line[:match.start()]+'______'+line[match.end():]
            decoy=next(w for w in t['blend'] if w.lower()!=chosen.lower())
            t['cloze']=dict(sentence=cloze,answer=actual,distractor=decoy)
            records.append(dict(id=t['id'],target=t['target'],known_vowels=''.join(sorted(known)),
                                sentence_count=len(t['sentences']),word_count=len(words(passage)),
                                sentence_word_counts=[len(words(s)) for s in t['sentences']],
                                heart_words=hearts,max_word_length=max(map(len,words(passage))),
                                consonants=''.join(sorted(set(passage.lower())&set('bcdfghjklmnpqrstvwxyz')))))
    assert len(set(alltexts))==36
    (ROOT/'decoding_audit.json').write_text(json.dumps(records,indent=2))

def txt(x,y,s,size=13,font='Body',color=INK,align='left'):
    s=str(s);width=pdfmetrics.stringWidth(s,font,size)
    left=x if align=='left' else x-width/2 if align=='center' else x-width
    assert left>=27 and left+width<=W-27,(BOOK,PAGE,s,left,width)
    C.setFillColor(color);C.setFont(font,size)
    if align=='center':C.drawCentredString(x,y,s)
    elif align=='right':C.drawRightString(x,y,s)
    else:C.drawString(x,y,s)
    LINE_BOXES.append(dict(book=BOOK,page=PAGE,text=s,x=left,y=y,width=width,size=size))

    style=ParagraphStyle('p',fontName='Body',fontSize=size,leading=size*1.42,textColor=color)
    p=Paragraph(s,style);_,height=p.wrap(width,1000)

def box(x,y,w,h,fill=PALE,stroke=None,r=11):
    C.setFillColor(fill);C.setStrokeColor(stroke or fill);C.setLineWidth(.6)
    C.roundRect(x,y,w,h,r,fill=1,stroke=int(stroke is not None))


def art(name,x,y,w,h,rounded=True):

# Book 0 - Combined Learner Book

90 A4 pages. Combines the original Book 0 teaching/practice material with the eight I Can Read picture passages. The existing 80-page PDF is preserved byte-for-byte as ECCR_Book_0-pre.pdf; its original cover still says Book 0 because its contents have not been edited. Its original review notes are preserved as ECCR_Book_0-pre_Yaw_Review.md.

## Page map

| PDF pages | Printed pages | Content |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1-2 | Unnumbered | Combined Book 0 cover and inside title |
| 3-73 | 1-71 | Original routine, teacher guidance, Twi vowels, core consonants, blending, reviews and optional digraph extension |
| 74-79 | 72-77 | Original English Bridge; final navigation now points to I Can Read |
| 80 | 78 | New English reading-readiness page |
| 81-88 | 79-86 | Eight I Can Read picture passages |
| 89 | 87 | Reader teacher guidance, with updated page references |
| 90 | Unnumbered | Single combined-series colophon |

## Important teaching gates

This remains a teacher-review draft, not a validated standardized programme or a research baseline test. Yaw must confirm the Twi sound inventory, sound values, word-picture prompts, formation and meanings described in the original review notes. The selected core consonants m, f, s, b, k, n remain provisional.

The English reader is not automatically accessible after short-a practice alone. Before assigning it, teach/confirm the English short vowels a, e, i, o, u, the consonants used, final consonant groups such as milk and fits, doubled letters such as egg and off, and word-ending s. Explicitly teach a, the, is, has, to, by, he and puts as needed. Select stories according to each learner's actual taught correspondences and readiness, not page order alone.

Every word in the eight reader story titles and passages is at most four letters. Short word length alone does not prove decodability. Each reader page has one illustration and five or six connected sentences; Yaw's Kim example is unchanged. No worksheets were added to the reader section.

## Preservation and production

- The earlier Book 0 is renamed, not deleted or rewritten. It can be restored from the -pre file at any time.
- The two standalone I Can Read PDFs and Books 1-9 remain unchanged.
- Duplicate reader cover, inside title and closing page are omitted from the combined edition; the original Book 0 closing page is replaced by one combined colophon.
- Original teaching pages PDF 3-78 are pixel-identical to the previous Book 0. PDF 79 only has its onward navigation updated.
- Printed folios run continuously from 1 to 87; odd on the right, even on the left. Covers and colophon are unnumbered.
- PDF bookmarks provide navigation between learning sections and all eight stories.
- 90 pages are suitable for an even-page A4 duplex sequence. Printer-specific imposition, spine width and bleed are not included.
- Source and QA files: ../a4/book0_combined_20260919/.

name: Deploy static ECCR app to GitHub Pages

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write

concurrency:
  group: pages
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  deploy:
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Setup Pages
        uses: actions/configure-pages@v5
      - name: Upload artifact
        uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3
        with:
          path: .
      - name: Deploy to GitHub Pages
        id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v4
